title: Dividing 3- to 4-Digit Numbers by 1-Digit and 2- to 3-Digit Numbers by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Division Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Divide two numbers with and without regrouping: 3- to 4-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, and 2- to 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers; estimate the quotient when dividing 3- to 4-digit dividends by 1- to 2-digit divisors, by first estimating the dividends and divisors using multiples of 10.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 division worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: long division by 1-digit and 2-digit numbers, zeros in the quotient, remainders and estimating quotients. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The remainder is always less than the divisor.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Long division: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat for each digit.
  • If a place cannot be divided, write 0 in the quotient.
  • The remainder must be less than the divisor. Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend.
  • To estimate, round the divisor to a multiple of 10 and change the dividend to a nearby number it divides easily.

Examples

Example

4,236 ÷ 6

42 hundreds ÷ 6 = 7 hundreds

3 tens ÷ 6 = 0 tens (write 0)

36 ÷ 6 = 6

Answer: 706

Example

Estimate 738 ÷ 23

23 → 20, 738 → 800

800 ÷ 20

Answer: about 40

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out a 0Write 0 when a place cannot be divided.
A remainder as big as the divisorThen the quotient digit is too small.
Rounding only the divisorChange the dividend to a compatible number too.

faq.q: How do I check a division?
faq.a: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder.
Numbers that are close to the real ones and easy to divide in your head.
